name: Nexus
notes: Simple mode now opens without Home/Away, developer, or Life360 setup controls. Those controls live together in the Advanced private room and remain local to the phone.

Nexus can foreground-open the installed Life360 app only after your tap, so Jay can complete Life360's own sign-in. Nexus never receives or retains its password, verification code, coordinates, maps, routes, or family trail.
The performance display now keeps the last hash-valid completed seven-stage native audit visible while a new poll is in flight; incomplete runtime begin-states cannot replace that timing map.

The phone functional-room rail now reconciles partial command snapshots against all eight canonical Hermes lanes, so Multi Bets or another lane cannot silently disappear while the native 112-cell mesh remains complete.

Physical release certification now honors an explicitly requested, online Samsung Wi-Fi transport even while the same handset is also attached by USB; unrequested multiple-handset ambiguity still fails closed.

Samsung Wi-Fi updates can now be enrolled without returning to USB: Android's one-time pairing code is bound to the previously hash-accepted physical Samsung serial, hardware, build fingerprint, and live Android identity before hidden reconnect is armed.

The wireless bridge accepts exactly one private-LAN ADB TLS handset, reuses an already connected session when mDNS is quiet, and rejects tampered acceptance evidence, another phone, emulator, public endpoint, ambiguous services, or identity drift; Hermes receives no shell or financial authority.

Hermes now runs a separate four-model prospective learning tournament across BTC, ETH, and SOL, increasing untouched directional evidence collection without changing the incumbent model or accelerating the independent-day clock.

Every challenger is frozen before outcomes, starts only after installation, uses deterministic discovery and confirmation UTC-day cohorts, and is evaluated with Bonferroni family-wise error control plus a 98.75% per-model uncertainty floor.

A challenger can become human-review eligible only after passing sample, day, symbol, direction, baseline, and multiplicity-adjusted uncertainty gates in both cohorts; automatic promotion, model mutation, recommendations, bets, orders, economic proof, and live authority remain sealed.

Hermes now parses and SHA-256 validates each retained mobile-history row once per learning cycle, then shares a centrally constructed read-only row view with source-health learning, prospective skill, venue-cost research, and prospective economics instead of reparsing the same multi-megabyte ledger four times.

The mobile learning receipt exposes single-pass-row-hash-v1, exact validated and rejected prior-row counts, one parse pass, and all five bounded consumers; native and external strict audits fail closed if validation is skipped, duplicated, incomplete, or rejects any row.

Legacy direct learner entry points still route through the same central row-hash validator, while retention, quarantine, checkpoint, paper-only, read-only, no-live-order, immutable-model, and economic-proof boundaries remain unchanged.

The performance governor now keeps the last fully completed hash-valid receipt authoritative while a new poll is in flight; a partial begin-state can no longer overwrite completed evidence or make strict self-audit fail spuriously.

History integrity repair now uses an exact SHA-256, byte-size, modification-time, installed-version, and self-test-bound checkpoint fast path, avoiding a full retained-history JSON reparse when every sealed input still matches.

Any history byte, size, timestamp, app-version, receipt, or self-test drift still forces complete row validation and bounded repair; corruption protection and all paper-only, read-only, and no-live-order safeguards remain unchanged.

Hermes now measures seven complete native poll stages: history repair, primary Crypto, parallel lanes, receipt persistence, snapshot assembly, bounded computation, and history-learning; missing, duplicate, malformed, unsafe, or partial timing inventories fail closed.

The performance governor retains hash-valid per-stage p50 and p95 trends across its bounded 32-run memory, allowing Hermes to identify the real tail bottleneck instead of assuming the slowest network lane caused the whole poll delay.

The phone Observatory visibly shows 7/7 verified stages, the slowest current stage, the slowest learned p95 stage, and each stage's last, median, p95, and observation count without granting prediction, betting, execution, or economic authority.

Hermes now records hash-bound duration, retry, completion, and fail-closed diagnostics for all nine native collection tasks; strict self-audit rejects missing, duplicate, malformed, unsafe, or incomplete diagnostic inventories.

Verified per-lane runtimes are retained in bounded history and used only as a longest-observed-task-first tie-break when source-health priority is equal, reducing parallel makespan without skipping any of the eight declared lanes.
Latency learning remains scheduling-order-only and cannot override full-lane coverage, retries, source evidence, battery, thermal, memory, storage, paper-only, read-only, or live-order safeguards.

Hermes notifications now use NTFY as the single phone alert owner while Nexus keeps a silent in-app copy and alerts only when NTFY delivery fails; duplicate device records cannot re-alert or reset read state.

Routine HOLD, ABSTAIN, fixture, count, and fingerprint churn stays silent; routine progress is capped to one daily digest, repeated urgent warnings use a two-hour cooldown, and true safety or activation changes remain immediate.

Phone messages now name the exact change in short Changed, Meaning, Next, and Status sections, while all eight room services publish only meaningful decision, source-health, evidence-milestone, or safety transitions.

Hermes paper-lifecycle reconciliation now binary-seeks exact observation windows instead of rescanning the full retained market history for every intent, removing the proof-scale timeout without weakening chronology or receipt checks.

A lifecycle-specific process lease now prevents the scheduler and autonomous-growth paths from concurrently parsing and overwriting the same append-only evidence state; overlapping invocations retain the active owner and exit safely.
Hermes now recomputes the native phone-app bridge receipt SHA-256 before accepting the capability, so altered bridge metadata fails closed instead of passing on hash shape alone.

Notification-listener discovery now matches an exact Android package component, preventing similarly named packages from impersonating the Nexus listener; NTFY mode also distinguishes observation, launch-only, and not-installed states.

Transient native provider retries now wait through a deterministic 500-1499 ms provider-specific stagger before the existing single retry, reducing synchronized burst failures without adding retries, promoting stale data, or weakening freshness gates.

Hermes lane-health learning now aggregates every receipt for a lane: a fresh public source keeps the lane observable, while missing account-fee or bookmaker evidence remains independently failed closed instead of corrupting the whole lane's learning status.

The corrected aggregate-fresh-precedence-v2 policy preserves legacy hash-stamped history but excludes pre-fix first-receipt labels from future source-health scheduling, preventing weeks of inherited false weakness.

The release verifier can now capture a sanitized native source diagnostic containing exact lane status, provider, bounded error, adaptive schedule, self-audit failures, and paper-safety state without exposing credentials or enabling execution.

The phone Observatory now shows the exact learned eight-lane collection order, source-health evidence count, full-coverage seal, recent poll success ledger, and rolling p95 runtime so adaptation is visible instead of hidden inside native receipts.

Hermes source-health learning now actively orders the next bounded native poll so historically weak lanes receive first access to concurrency and deadline headroom; the hash-validated schedule must still run every declared lane and has no prediction, betting, execution, or economic authority.

Hermes now retains a bounded, hash-validated 32-run performance memory with success rate and latency percentiles; degraded history can only reduce concurrency into recovery mode and can never override battery, thermal, memory, storage, evidence, or trading safeguards.
The phone learning curriculum now preserves the venue ledger's real 100-observation and 5-independent-UTC-day gates, so rapid repeated scans cannot make public cost research appear complete.

Multi Bets now retains a fresh, hash-bound Australian public fixture-context receipt when device-bound bookmaker credentials are absent, keeping all eight lanes operational without presenting fixtures as odds, probability, edge, stake, recommendation, or betting authority.

Every new invested phone-native economics trial now binds its exact contemporaneous BTC, ETH, or SOL account-fee receipt when available; the sanitized receipt hash and fee-source mode are frozen before the outcome without retaining credentials or enabling orders.

Economic acceptance now requires a Student-t paired daily lower bound above gross buy-and-hold and remains positive at twice the modelled transaction cost, preventing a fragile point estimate or optimistic fee assumption from turning green.
Phone readiness now separates 8/8 declared lane receipts from genuinely fresh working lanes; an unavailable fail-closed lane can no longer look healthy merely because its receipt exists.

The attached-device verifier now binds every native self-audit to a unique request ID, completes its read-only handoff off the Android main thread, and tolerates bounded handset-to-PC clock skew without accepting an older request.

The native self-audit now re-evaluates app bridges, self-build planning, and operational self-awareness in one cycle, preventing a newly installed or removed bridge from leaving contradictory stale capability states.

Hermes Messages room taps now switch immediately, update the Ask Hermes room, expose an aria-pressed selection, and visibly highlight the selected room card instead of relying on a long smooth scroll.
A repeatable release-emulator UI audit now exercises all eight message-room jumps plus all 112 lane-to-functional-room selections while preserving an explicit emulator-only evidence boundary.
Phone-native lane collection now isolates every provider behind one shared bounded completion deadline, so a single slow source cannot suppress already-completed lane receipts.
Each lane receives at most one retry for transient network, HTTP 408/425/429, and server failures; permanent failures remain unavailable and stale receipts are never relabelled fresh.
Timed-out, interrupted, and unexpected lane failures now retain their declared lane identity and emit an explicit fail-closed receipt while collection continues for the other lanes.
The native all-lane command now enumerates all eight Luminaris lanes, including Multi Bets, so phone readiness and repair counts no longer collapse to seven.
Verified device-bound bookmaker consensus now contributes only to Multi Bets source-foundation health; calibrated edge, expected value, staking, betting, and profit authority remain sealed.
The physical-device self-audit now fails closed unless it observes the one-retry policy, bounded lane deadline, all eight native command lanes, and an explicit no-stale-promotion seal.

The obsolete Firebase Admin test path and its six moderate transitive advisories were removed from the build dependency graph; Nexus-local receipt-backed phone notifications remain the active transport.
Android WebView navigation now forces a native-only compositor repaint after route, lane, and connected-room state changes, fixing taps that updated the DOM but left the previous screen visible.

All eight Luminaris lane cards and all fourteen same-lane functional-room cards now use explicit verified handlers; room selection moves focus to the active detail panel and announces the selected receipt context.
Swipe-based character-room navigation remains removed; the fixed top-left back button is still the only room-exit gesture.
PC and phone dashboards now require the committed v511 Multis probability-semantics bridge, preventing a stale v510 client from silently accepting the corrected contract.

The signed Multis v2 receipt separates bookmaker marketConsensusProbabilityPct from independent modelProbabilityPct; all 524 current market-consensus combinations have null independent-model probability and null edge.
Multis now retains every observed offer up to an explicit 2,000-offer ceiling and fails closed before publication on overflow instead of silently truncating an unreproducible receipt.

Sports player evidence now reports twelve exact accounting sub-gates and binds AFL statistics-derived roster identities only to their exact AFL competition, preventing NRL rows from crossing receipt authority.
Live v511 telemetry verifies all eight isolated rooms as healthy and adaptive while preserving the honest 0/8 untouched-skill result and sealed betting, staking, execution, and live-order authority.
The phone now computes a hash-bound per-event bookmaker consensus by removing each bookmaker's overround before averaging probabilities, with dispersion and source count retained for every selection.

Mobile odds consensus is explicitly market-probability context only: it is not an independent Hermes model, executable multi price, calibrated edge, expected value, stake, recommendation, execution receipt, or profit proof.

The PC Sports collector refreshes event-bound official context even when player-history evidence is safely cached; current context coverage remains explicit per combination and incomplete rows continue to lower Multis readiness.
Hermes can now receive research explicitly shared from GitHub, ChatGPT, Claude, Notion, or another Android app into a private hash-stamped inbox; no app-private data is read automatically.

Every shared research item remains quarantined for human review with bounded storage, duplicate suppression, and credential-pattern rejection; it cannot train models, become economic proof, recommend a bet, place an order, or move money.

Hermes now creates a hash-stamped on-device self-build plan that targets the active weakest-proof lesson, permits one bounded proposal, and can correctly decide that no rebuild is justified while untouched outcomes are pending.

Self-build is now a verified proposal and reviewed-handoff capability, and self-design is operational with rollback and untouched verification required; source mutation, signing, deployment, silent installation, self-promotion, and financial authority remain sealed.

The phone app bridge map now includes installed GitHub, ChatGPT, Claude, and Notion handoffs alongside NTFY, Termux, Exchange, calendars, and sharing without reading conversations, repositories, credentials, or private app storage.
Hermes now inventories bounded NTFY, Termux, Crypto.com Exchange, calendar, and Android share-sheet handoffs on the phone; app-private data, arbitrary commands, and financial authority remain sealed.

Hermes can now receive Crypto.com Exchange and Sports Odds credentials through a one-time RSA/AES encrypted USB envelope and store them behind the handset Android Keystore; plaintext secrets never enter the APK, feed, logs, receipts, or history.
The phone now verifies account tier and exact BTC, ETH, and SOL fee rates using an exact three-method read allowlist with balances, orders, withdrawals, acknowledgements, and fills excluded.

Multi Bets now has an Australia-first device-bound h2h odds source with current bookmaker and quote counts, while independent model probability, calibrated edge, expected value, staking, recommendations, execution, and profit claims remain sealed.

Hermes now runs a hash-stamped weakness-directed self-teaching curriculum with eight explicit lessons spanning economics, execution, directional skill, fees, Multi Bets, lane health, venue costs, and autonomous continuity.
Each curriculum cycle distinguishes routine operational evidence from genuinely new untouched outcomes; first-run history establishes a baseline and cannot be relabelled as new learning.

The native self-audit, physical-device verifier, operational self-awareness receipt, and phone Observatory now require the frozen curriculum while keeping model mutation, backfill, code mutation, profit claims, bets, and live orders sealed.
Hermes now maintains a hash-stamped operational self-awareness receipt covering all twelve requested capability families, explicit limitations, unknowns, and ranked weakest proof.

The phone Observatory and physical-device audit now require this self-awareness contract while explicitly rejecting consciousness, profit, prediction-authority, autonomous code-mutation, and live-trading claims.
Hermes Observatory now orders overlapping native self-audit reads and retries cold-launch hydration boundedly so an older fail-closed result cannot overwrite a newer verified receipt.
Failed native self-audits now list every failed check and use an explicit failed-closed boundary instead of describing an unverified receipt as verified.
Hermes now keeps a bounded hash-stamped autonomous continuity ledger for real phone-side polling attempts, successes, failures, triggers, and observed gaps.
Hermes re-arms its persisted market and updater jobs after cold launch, boot, user unlock, and app replacement, and repairs either schedule if Android drops it.
The mobile self-audit and physical-device verifier now require autonomous continuity while preserving scheduling-only authority and sealed trading gates.
The React, package, and Android version identities are locked by a regression check so future update receipts cannot compare against a stale embedded version.
Hermes now freezes one prospective long-or-cash spot economics trial per UTC day and scores it after modeled venue costs against cash and gross BTC/ETH/SOL buy-and-hold.
Crypto.com public-book observations now estimate spread, depth, and conservative published-fee hurdles without impersonating account-specific fees, fills, profit, or live readiness.
Hermes now emits the compact sanitized native self-audit handoff whenever the native audit receipt is rebuilt, allowing a release handset to be audited after cold launch.
Hermes Observatory now uses the native self-audit provenance receipt when the projection snapshot is stale, so source ownership cannot show a false unverified state.
Hermes standalone verification now requires Android-native source provenance and an explicitly unconfigured PC endpoint; mixed or PC-fed snapshots remain unverified.
Hermes mobile self-audit now requires complete receipt and Nexus-local read-back coverage for all eight declared Luminaris lanes; partial meshes remain unverified.
The Luminaris Observatory can now share the exact sanitized native self-audit JSON from the phone, giving physical-device verification a user-controlled handoff without PC storage or NTFY.
Native Hermes collection and status reads now refresh the durable self-audit, so a post-update receipt cannot retain the previous installed-version state.

Hermes now runs a native on-device self-audit and records PC independence, native collection/computation, Nexus-local notifications, cellular updater safety, and the explicit physical-handset evidence boundary.
A required newer build now opens Update Center as the startup route from both the durable native receipt and the fresh cellular check; the gate cannot be hidden by a remembered Home route.
Hermes and the cellular updater now run through protected Android JobScheduler workers, keeping multi-source background work outside BroadcastReceiver time limits.
The PC bridge installer now accepts a masked token prompt, stores only a DPAPI-protected token, and keeps it out of the scheduled-task command line.
Command pages now return to the Pantheon Gateway with truthful route labels, and the Backup Setup surface is covered by a runtime regression guard.
Nexus keeps the mandatory Update Center and native Hermes Observatory in the initial app graph so cold launches cannot stall behind a lazy chunk; secondary pages remain isolated.
Hades Vault now supports encrypted OpenAlex credentials with a redacted, session-only Mimir consumer and a focused secure-intake screen.
Mimir can search OpenAlex for source-backed scholarly evidence without persisting the API key, query, or result receipt.
Heimdall can load CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities from CISA's official GitHub mirror with validated defensive receipts and fail-closed errors.
The high-severity Netlify image parser advisory chain is removed by pinning the last unaffected compatible receipt adapter.
Every character room now renders its profile portrait prominently in the room header on desktop and phone layouts.
All 15 character rooms now have profile imagery, installed engines, and honest readiness states.
Zeus, Amun-Ra, Ares, Poseidon, Gabriel, and Phoenix now have purpose-built working dashboards.
Amun-Ra can request on-demand Open-Meteo weather and UV context without storing device coordinates.
Hades Vault now uses authenticated AES-256-GCM encryption and session-only secret unlocks.
The PC Backup Bridge now fails closed on LAN, requires authenticated health and copy requests, and writes atomic receipts.
Nexus now enforces a restrictive content security policy and same-origin executable scripts.
Nexus Android now uses current package, usage-access, notification-text, and APK-install APIs while preserving the proven Gmail consent flow.
Backup Setup now uses a native Android PC Backup Bridge for health checks and backup copy before falling back to WebView fetch.
Nexus release packaging now defaults to the free GitHub raw manifest and GitHub Releases APK path.
Update Center now shows feed behind when the installed app is newer than the public release feed.
Release package verification now checks that the local manifest and APK target the GitHub feed correctly.
